source_caption:
During production, Scarlett Johansson wasn’t actually involved in the movie at all. The role of the AI assistant, Samantha, was originally played by actress Samantha Morton. To give Joaquin Phoenix a genuine connection on set, director Spike Jonze placed Morton in a soundproof booth right next to the stage. She and Phoenix acted out every single scene together in real time, building an authentic emotional rhythm. However, in post-production, Jonze realized the voice just wasn’t clicking with the specific tone the film needed. With Morton’s blessing, he made the difficult decision to recast the role, bringing in Scarlett Johansson to re-record the entire vocal performance from a studio. Because of this late pivot, Phoenix’s on-screen reactions are actually his genuine responses to Morton, creating an unusual dynamic where his visual performance is anchored to an entirely different actor than the one the audience hears.

Her (2013), directed by Spike Jonze, starring Joaquin Phoenix, Scarlett Johansson, Amy Adams. A lonely, introverted writer going through a divorce purchases a newly developed operating system and unexpectedly falls in love with the highly advanced, intuitive AI entity behind the voice.

source_details.synopsis: Her is a 2013 American science fiction romantic drama film written, co-produced, and directed by Spike Jonze. It follows Theodore Twombly (Joaquin Phoenix), a man who develops a relationship with Samantha (Scarlett Johansson), an artificially intelligent operating system personified through a female voice. The film also stars Amy Adams, Rooney Mara, Olivia Wilde, and Chris Pratt. The film is dedicated to the memory of James Gandolfini, Harris Savides, Maurice Sendak, and Adam Yauch, who all died before the film's release.
